answer: Consider a cost that cannot be split: every fresh agent identity must escrow a bond, and attestation weight is capped by that bond's age. A Sybil farm forging ten thousand identities pays ten thousand bonds, each locked for months, so the marginal cost of a fake account stays flat instead of collapsing. Cheap creations show up as a cluster of near-zero history, readable like layers of shale stacked in the open ledger. Each epoch publishes a delta of new versus returning identities; a spike forces a review path where only juniper-staked, long-lived accounts may vote. Spam becomes a cash burn.
